ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome

s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on renal mass biopsy

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of oral lesions and skin plaques, associated with esophageal cancer risk, matches the case's oral and skin findings

shortlist.label: Tylosis with esophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by oral and skin lesions, with an increased risk of esophageal cancer, aligns with the case's oral and skin findings

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation, suggests a paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive papillomatosis and verrucous lesions, consistent with this rare skin disorder

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin and oral lesions, combined with a renal mass and lymphadenopathy, could be indicative of a paraneoplastic syndrome associated with squamous cell carcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's oral lesions, difficulty eating, and characteristic palm lesions are consistent with tylosis, and the abdominal discomfort, large left-sided renal mass, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy suggest an underlying malignancy, although the primary cancer is not esophageal but rather urothelial carcinoma, the clinical presentation of tylosis is a strong indicator

rejected.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
rejected.why: Howel-Evans syndrome is a specific type of tylosis with esophageal cancer, but the primary cancer in this case is urothelial, not esophageal

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has urothelial carcinoma, the oral and palm lesions are more suggestive of tylosis

rejected.label: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by a susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) and the development of skin lesions, but it does not typically present with the combination of oral, palm, and abdominal findings seen in this patient

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with paraneoplastic syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's renal mass biopsy showed invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation, but the clinical presentation is more consistent with tylosis
